To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

Temporal Convolution Networks are a promising class of architectures for 3D action recognition, Res-TCNs are state-of-the-art on NTU RGB+D dataset, Res-TCNS are interpretable, and we can learn interpretable spatio temporal representations for 3d human action recognition.
Temporal Convolution Neural Networks (TCNs) are a powerful tool for interpretable 3D human recognition.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions: 1) How to use a new model, TCN for 3D Human action recognition?
the following three questions: (i) How to use Temporal Convolution Networks to perform 3D human activity recognition?

• Proposing an interpretable 3D human representation using a Temporal Convolution Network (TCN), • Using TCN to achieve state-of-the-art performance on the largest human action recognition dataset NTU-RGB, • Using the interpretability of TCN to understand the learned representations.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed method, Res-TCNs, is a state-of-the-art model for 3D action recognition, and that it is the first interpretable deep learning model for 3d human action analysis.
we present a novel interpretable deep learning model, Res- TCN, for 3D skeleton-based human action recognition.
we have proposed a novel model for 3D Human action recognition, which is interpretable, and achieves state-of-the- art results on NTU-RGB-D, the largest 3-D Human action recognition dataset.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

(1) we introduce the first interpretable 3D human representation model that is able to achieve state-of-the-art performance on 3D human activity recognition, (2) we show that the interpretability of TCN can provide a way to understand and explain how the model learns the spatio-temporal patterns of 3D actions, and (3) we show that TCN can be used to learn interpretable spatio- temporal representations for 3d human action recognition.
we have developed a model that is interpretable, and yet achieves state-of-the art results for 3D skeleton based human action recognition.
we present a novel approach for 3D spatio-temporal action recognition that can provide a way to understand and interpret the inner workings of a learning-based method.
The main takeaway from our work is that
interpretable models can be competitive to black-box models, and can be a useful tool for understanding the inner workings of the learning process in deep learning models.
interpretable models can be just as accurate as the state-of-the-art black-box models, while providing a much deeper understanding of how the model makes its decisions.
interpretable spatio temporal representations for 3d human action recognition can be learnt with TCNs.
